sections.body: Pittsburgh sends extra rushers on 28.2% of dropbacks [dc1] over 386 plays [dc2], with a pressure proxy of 14.8% [dc3] and a sack rate of 7.8% [dc4] that ranks 7th [dc5]. Denver's protection should expect regular blitzes, so hot throws and quick game are the best counter. Opponents succeed on 42.9% of plays [dc7] and produce explosive plays on 8.5% [dc8] across 597 plays [dc9]. The explosive-play rate is the main warning sign for Denver's deep shots. On third down Pittsburgh allows conversions on 33.6% [dc14] over 125 plays [dc15], while Denver converts 34.1% [dc16] over 123 plays [dc17], a near-even matchup decided by the calls. In the red zone Pittsburgh has allowed touchdowns on 47.8% of drives [dc18] over 23 drives [dc19], and Denver has scored on 67.7% [dc20] over 31 drives [dc21], a real threat near the goal line.

sections.heading: Special teams
sections.body: Chris Boswell has made 22 [kc1] of 27 [kc2] field goals (81.5% [kc3]), but his long range is the soft spot at 62.5% [kc4] on 8 [kc5] long tries. Treat a long attempt as a coin flip in a close late game. Kickoffs are rarely touchbacks at 16.0% [kc9] on 50 [kc10] kickoffs, and the coverage allows 27.4 [kc11] yards per return on 40 [kc12] returns. Denver returns kickoffs for 26.1 [kc13] yards on 35 [kc14] returns, so kick away from that returner unless a touchback is likely. Pittsburgh's special-teams EPA of -0.02 [kc15] ranks 22nd [kc16], against Denver's 0.04 [kc17], which ranks 6th [kc18].

sections.heading: Key matchups
sections.body: First, Denver's protection against Pittsburgh's pressure: the Steelers send extra rushers on 28.2% of dropbacks [mc1] over 386 plays [mc2]. Denver should lean on quick game and backs in protection. Second, Pittsburgh's medium-distance passing against Denver's coverage: the Steelers throw on 72.1% of medium-distance plays [mc4] over 111 plays [mc5], and Metcalf takes 21.8% of targets [mc6]. Safety Brandon Jones is Questionable after a 90.8% snap share [mc8] over 8 games [mc9], so Denver needs a ready replacement. Third, the red zone: Denver has scored on 67.7% of red-zone drives [mc10] over 31 drives [mc11], and Pittsburgh has allowed touchdowns on 47.8% [mc12] over 23 drives [mc13]. Fourth, kicking: Boswell is 62.5% [mc16] on long tries over 8 attempts [mc17], while Pittsburgh kickoffs are touchbacks only 16.0% [mc18] over 50 kickoffs [mc19].
